findings.reason: a node told to edit a rubric list inside `_run_open` must either fail to locate it or invent a branch, and the plan's "one derivation" claim would rest on an edit no reader can find.
findings.text: §5 says a failed check becomes a blocking finding "with rubric `domain`" and that `review_lifecycle`'s `_run_open` reads it "once the rubric list it branches on includes `domain`"; `_run_open` (`reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py:124`) branches on no rubric list at all — it delegates to `_blocking`, which reads the finding's `severity` against `NON_BLOCKING_SEVERITIES = frozenset({"follow-on"})` (line 74), and the only `rubric` references in that file (`:235`) are the review *subject* discriminator for figure reviews — so the edit the plan names does not exist, and the real requirement is that the finding be stored with a blocking severity (no change to `_run_open`); as written the node is sent to extend a rubric list it will not find and may add a spurious rubric branch to compensate

findings.reason: the implementing node must either break the documented purity contract (and the no-repository synthesised-node path) or move the check to the caller, neither of which the plan states.
findings.text: §6 puts the new `inputs` check inside `judge_prescribed` ("The two checks become properties in that judgement") and requires a node "whose repository-path inputs do not exist" be refused, but `judge_prescribed(node)` (`reckon/crew/prescription.py:130`) takes the node and nothing else while the module's own docstring declares the judgement pure — "computable before any worktree, plan file or flight configuration exists" and "a caller can judge a synthesised node with no repository" — and `TaskNode` (`reckon/crew/node.py:724`) carries no repository root, so the check has no base to resolve "repository-path inputs" against and the plan never names one; the done-when ("refused at dispatch with the path, and the same node with the file present dispatches") therefore cannot be produced by the mechanism as placed

findings.reason: a node told this trust boundary is new will build fresh execution and logging rather than reuse the established re-run path, changing the guard's surface and its estimate.
findings.text: §4 says the new promotion guard "is the first guard that executes a repository-declared command, which is a different trust boundary from the guards that read a run's own recorded evidence", but promotion already executes a flight-declared command under a bounded timeout: the integration re-run in `reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:787` runs `subprocess.run(["sh", "-c", replayed], cwd=…, timeout=bound_seconds)` on the recorded gate command, which §4's own sibling mechanism arms from `gates.suite_command` in the repository's `flight.yaml` (`reckon/crew/promotion_records.py:347`); the plan also asserts "Surface: … one guard" without acknowledging the existing worktree-root rewriting and replay-log convention that path already carries

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every cited anchor resolves at `866fb9bf`: `_run_open` (`reckon/crew/review_lifecycle.py:124`), `dispatch_review_for_run` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2056`), `blocking_finding_dispositions` (`reckon/crew/repair.py:242`), `gates.dimension_floors` (`reckon/_flight_schema.py:620`), `_brief_record`/`_brief_text` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2015,2026`), `judge_prescribed`/`PRESCRIBED_PROPERTIES` (`reckon/crew/prescription.py:130,46`), `TaskNode` (`reckon/crew/node.py:724`), `REVIEW_DIMENSIONS`/`REVIEW_ITEMS` (`reckon/crew/review.py:89,108`), acceptance floor (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:24`), `docs/_shared/flight.schema.json`, and the `docs/state/<project>/flight.yaml` convention (`reckon/flight.py:481`).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each of §2–§6 declares a negative control that can fail: §2 "on the base commit the first fixture dispatches a review, and the test fails there", §3 "nothing for a project without the block", §4 "without the declaration the same fixture promotes", §5 "a project without declarations scores six dimensions … the acceptance floor is unchanged", §6 "a project that declares no `model_paths` is never linted".
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-whens gate in pytest, and §7 writes its replay results to the landed record with run ids; no gate log is placed in a scratchpad or node-local temp path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new symbols (`rules_for`, `domain`, `inputs`, `compares_with`) are named by mechanism, and no plan label.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — §5 names a rubric branch `_run_open` does not have; §6 places a filesystem check in a judgement documented as pure with no repository root; §4 overstates the novelty of executing a repository-declared command.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one capability; §4's brief-side and guard-side are the two halves of one wiring (`rules_for` into dispatch and into promotion), reviewed on one verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `plan-section-depends-on` resolves every edge to a node that exists (s4/s5/s6→s3, s7→s2,s4,s5,s6), `plan-after: scoring-should-stop-a-promotion` resolves to `docs/plans/scoring-should-stop-a-promotion.html`, and no section reads a unit it does not depend on.
